note: The consonants dn'l (as in 14:14) point to Danel, the wise and just king of Ugaritic legend, rather than the exile Daniel, a younger contemporary of Ezekiel.

kjv: Thou (the king of Tyre) sealest up the sum
mine: You (the king of Tyre) were the seal of perfection
note: hotem toknit is a noun phrase "a seal (signet) of proportion/perfection" describing the king as a model of perfection, not a verb "you seal up the sum".

kjv: the workmanship of thy (the king of Tyre's) tabrets and of thy pipes
mine: your (the king of Tyre's) settings and your mountings were crafted in gold
note: tuppim and neqavim here are jeweller's terms (settings and sockets for the stones just listed); KJV read them as drums and pipes, introducing musical instruments into the description.

kjv: the sardius, topaz, and the diamond ... the carbuncle
note: The nine stones (a subset of the high priest's breastplate) are uncertain; yahalom cannot be diamond, which could not be engraved in antiquity, and the MT list has nine stones while KJV ends with "carbuncle" from barekat.
